results.notes:
Built the SPA half of WS10-S6 (code and unit tests), with no VITE_ flag. Section visibility follows the BFF reply to GET /api/v1/orgs/:id/model-entitlement ({enabled:false} gives a not-enabled note and no editor).

What exists:
- chat-client.ts: `listModelCatalogue()` returns {models, entitlement}, and `listModels()` is kept with the same signature as a wrapper over it. The entitlement meta is parsed whole or not at all. It is also exposed through `getModelEntitlementMeta()`, the same pattern as `getAttachmentPolicy`, so the composer, which already loads the catalogue through `listModels`, needs no second request and the roughly 20 existing composer test mocks of `listModels` are untouched. New pure helpers: `enforcedMaxEffort`, `effortLevelWithin`, `selectionIsStale`.
- DashboardComposer.tsx:
  - A pinned model the enforced policy no longer lists is replaced, by the policy default if the catalogue lists it and otherwise by Verevon Balance, with a visible notice, and the new choice is persisted.
  - The effort select drops options above `max_effort`: Quick maps to low, Deep to high, Max to xhigh, and Auto sends no effort so is never capped.
  - A pick made earlier falls to the strongest allowed level on send, with a notice.
  - Both rules apply only when `enforced` is true, so shadow mode changes nothing.
  - An empty catalogue (an outage) never resets a selection.
- AiModelPicker.tsx: the same stale-selection reset plus notice, so the Space, Support and Inbox pickers follow the policy.
- OrgModelAccessSection.tsx: editor for the org default and role overrides (allow mode, allow list, deny list, max effort). It saves with `expected_revision`, refuses an empty listed policy and `*` patterns client-side, and shows the typed refusals (revision_conflict, model_policy_leaves_no_zdr_model and others) through `translateApiError`. It preserves `min_privacy_tier` and `defaults` of an existing policy.
- errors.ts: the member refusals model_not_entitled and model_entitlement_unavailable render from `model-entitlement-refusals.ts` (Norwegian first), and the admin refusal codes were added.
- settings-sections.ts, WorkspaceSettingsPage.tsx, sidebar-navigation.ts: new 'model-access' section, route match and nav item. `applyDemoModeNavGate(sections, {modelAccessEnabled})` hides the nav item unless the BFF flag is passed, so with the existing call site the tab stays hidden.
- tests/e2e/model-entitlement.spec.ts: three route-stubbed cases (stale reset with notice, effort ceiling, Norwegian refusal on a denied pinned send). Written but NOT run: it needs the second dev server on 5174 and auth.

Decision for the lead: the nav item needs a cast (`MODEL_ACCESS_HREF`) because `VerevonRoute` lives in shell-data.ts, which is not owned. The shared edits below remove it. I did not run `pnpm test:e2e`.

results.notes:
What exists. The single gate is in memory_control.rs: MemoryState, MemoryAccess {Full, OrgOnly, None}, MemoryReason (on, user_paused, user_off, org_disabled, zdr, policy_unavailable), a pure decide(zdr, org, user) table, resolve (reader, unlocked read), resolve_in_tx (writer, FOR UPDATE row lock), stored_state, and set_state (bumps extract_after on a transition into on, writes a content-free memory_control_events row). permits_extraction now asks the gate under the same lock, so persist_candidates and apply_grounded_candidates are covered for both Dreaming and inline.

Writers gated: inline append (append_message_in_tx asks resolve_in_tx before persist or Letta), persist_candidates, apply_grounded_candidates, index_agent_memory (asks under the lock and returns the empty id on denial; the IndexMemory handler maps that to failed_precondition memory_not_enabled:<reason>). Dreaming load_pending_messages and load_preceding_context exclude non-on users.

Readers gated: SearchMemory (skip_reason, org-only rows while paused or off, Letta skipped), the context assembly in grpc.rs (access passed to load_agent_memory_context_rows; memory_index rows and the Letta mirror skipped unless Full), ListMemory (hidden_reason user_off or org_disabled; paused keeps the list). DeleteMemory is untouched.

New RPCs: GetMemoryControls (a ZDR caller is answered reason=zdr and nothing is read or written) and SetMemoryControls (user caller for themselves only; refused for a service, ZDR or waived credential; refused with failed_precondition when MEMORY_CONTROLS_ENABLED is off).

learning_events: SkippedMemoryState and SkippedOrigin (only threads.origin='chat'), counter mp_session_learning_run_events_skipped_total{reason}, both under the kill switch. gdpr purges memory_control_events.

model-gateway: three new prefetch outcome labels, the skip token mapping (skipped_prefetch_outcome), the gRPC twin records it, recall_memory returns {"memory":"unavailable","reason":...}. execution-core: save_memory maps memory_not_enabled:* to an honest tool error and recall_memory reports unavailable instead of no_memories.

Proto: only the plan's tags (SearchMemoryResponse.skip_reason=4, ListMemoryResponse.hidden_reason=4, MemoryControls 1-9, SetMemoryControlsRequest 1-3), all additive. The Get request and the two response wrappers are my own shapes; the plan did not specify them.

depth_findings.text: prost-generated pb::InferRequest derives Debug and would print image bytes if any caller logs a request with {:?}; the internal ImagePart redacts, the wire type does not. No grep for such a log was done.

vision_unsupported is not yet in the committed status contract golden, the gateway refusal catalogue or its trailer reader; a gateway reading the trailer treats it as an unknown FAILED_PRECONDITION until WS08-S4 and the golden regeneration land.
The vision denylist is name-based, so an operator-chosen Azure alias for a denylisted model over-advertises vision; the server gate only fails closed for names it recognises.
No test covers the intent-ladder substituting a non-vision rung for an image request, or the OpenAI unified-Azure flavor (supports_vision false) end to end.
Each image is base64-encoded on every attempt and retry; 4 images of up to 20 MB each make per-attempt memory large, and the 20 MB per-image cap is far above the gateway's planned 1 MB cap.

Anthropic apply_prompt_caching skips a last message that is an image block array, so image turns lose last-message caching; not measured, and the ZDR image path under Anthropic with tiered system is untested.
No magic-byte sniffing of image data against the declared mime type; a mismatch is passed to the provider, which rejects it.

Gateway side is not wired: the model-gateway refusal catalogue, trailer reader and sse-event-taxonomy do not know kind vision_unsupported, so it reads as an unknown FAILED_PRECONDITION; WS08-S4 must map it before any caller sets image_parts.

The prost-generated pb::InferRequest derives Debug and prints image bytes if any caller logs a request with {:?}; only the internal ImagePart redacts, so a grep of all pb::InferRequest log sites is needed before callers set image_parts.

The vision denylist is name-based, so an operator-chosen Azure deployment alias for a denylisted model over-advertises vision and passes the server gate; INFERENCE_VISION_MODEL_DENYLIST_EXTRA is the only mitigation.

No test covers the intent-ladder substituting a non-vision rung for an image request, the OpenAI unified-Azure flavor, or a streaming path with an image on the OpenAI/Anthropic adapters; the vision gate is also not applied at the embedding site (correct, since embeddings carry no images).

Each image is base64-encoded on every attempt and retry, and the 20 MB per-image cap with the 16 MiB decode limit is inconsistent: a single 20 MB image can never arrive through tonic (decode limit 16 MiB), so MAX_IMAGE_BYTES is unreachable for image parts and the effective cap is about 16 MiB total request.
Anthropic apply_prompt_caching skips a last message that is an image block array, so image turns lose last-message caching, and the tiered-system plus image combination is untested.
The no-image body byte-identity test covers only the OpenAI body; the Anthropic text-only body is covered only by pre-existing tests.
No magic-byte sniffing of image data against the declared mime type; a mismatch is passed through and rejected by the provider.
